name: Galaxie 500
label: Rough Trade
lede: Three Harvard kids made three albums in three years with one producer. Then Dean Wareham told Damon Krukowski not to buy the plane tickets to Japan.

eras.title: A borrowed kit and a studio in New York
eras.text: Wareham, Krukowski and Yang play Cambridge and Boston clubs and never sell one out on a weekend night. The records get made in New York, in a studio run by Kramer.

years.src: WBUR: Damon & Naomi Look Back To Galaxie 500 · Wikipedia: Galaxie 500
years.h: Yang buys a bass she can't play, and the band starts anyway
years.p: Dean Wareham and Damon Krukowski started the band at Harvard, with Krukowski on a drum kit lent by classmate Conan O'Brien. Naomi Yang bought a Gibson EB2 at Cambridge Music Center in Porter Square and learned on it.
years.xp:
[[Dean Wareham|a21a3ff2-064c-452d-8aea-3d4039ab70d6]] and Krukowski had been friends since their days at the Dalton School in New York City; the band came together while they were students at Harvard. The name came from a friend's Ford Galaxie 500.

Yang told WBUR she had no idea how to play bass when she started, and ended up playing high on the neck, lines you could sing along to. The band was never a draw at home: WBUR's write-up says they never sold out a club on a weekend night in Boston.

years.cap: Yang, Krukowski and Wareham in headphones at Kramer's Noise New York, c. 1988
years.src: Wikipedia: Galaxie 500 · Wikipedia: On Fire · Wikipedia: This Is Our Music
years.h: Kramer records the first single, then every record after it
years.p: Galaxie 500 cut Tugboat with [[Kramer|d898e082-70d1-4a86-ac8e-ecdf89892994]], the Shimmy Disc label boss, in February 1988. He produced everything they made.
years.xp: Kramer's Noise New York studio was home base for the next three years. He also played on the records himself: the credits list cheap organ on On Fire and cheap flute on This Is Our Music.

years.h: Today, cut in July at Noise New York
years.p: Kramer produced and engineered the debut for Aurora Records. A German CD followed in 1989, a Rough Trade US pressing in 1991.

years.h: CBGB, December 13, 1988, gets its own record in 2025
years.p: The band played the New York club that night. A recording was announced for 2025 as CBGB 12.13.88.
years.xp: The 2025 release follows Uncollected Noise New York '88-'90, an archival set that came out in 2024. The date comes straight from the release title.

eras.title: London says yes
eras.text: A Rough Trade contract, two Peel sessions, and an album that lands at number 7 on the UK indie chart.

years.h: A UK tour, and Rough Trade signs them
years.p: They toured Britain from late 1988 into 1989, and Rough Trade became the label for their next two albums.

yt: Don't Let Our Youth Go to Waste, Peel Session
years.h: Peel has them in twice, and his listeners vote a cover to number 41
years.p: Two sessions on BBC Radio 1. Their version of [[Jonathan Richman|bae34b81-9abd-416e-a720-fedc359df775]]'s Don't Let Our Youth Go to Waste placed 41st in the 1989 Festive 50.
years.xp: The Peel sessions were collected on the 2005 album Peel Sessions. The Richman song later lent its title to the 2004 two-disc DVD about the band.

years.h: On Fire hits number 7 on the UK indie chart
years.p: Kramer produced it again at Noise New York. Pitchfork gave it a 10 and ranked it number 16 on its 2002 list of the top 100 albums of the 1980s.
years.xp: UK critics loved it. US press was mixed, with some reviews citing Wareham's vocals as a limit. The Rolling Stone Album Guide later called it the band's best album by far.

eras.title: A hard record, and a tense tour
eras.text: This Is Our Music arrives in September, the last of the three. By Wareham's account, the fighting had already moved onto the road.

years.cap: Galaxie 500 on the main stage at Glastonbury, June 22, 1990
years.src: Wikipedia: This Is Our Music · Wikipedia: Galaxie 500
years.h: This Is Our Music is the last album, and Wareham calls it very difficult
years.p: Recorded at Noise New York with Kramer, who played flute. Yang sings lead on Listen, the Snow Is Falling.
years.xp: Wareham later said making it had been very difficult, and that Columbia Records had been interested in signing them. The album charted on the UK Independent Album Breakers list in 2010 after the reissues, at number 18.

years.src: On Some Bands That Don't Like Each Other I: The Breakup of Galaxie 500 · Dean Wareham : Black Postcards
yt: Ceremony, live at Club Lingerie, Los Angeles, 1990
years.h: On tour, Wareham and Krukowski fight over hotel rooms and who stands where
years.p: Wareham's memoir Black Postcards recalls friction over Krukowski's tour management: hotel rooms, seat assignments, and a Los Angeles show where Krukowski objected to where Wareham stood.
years.xp:
This account comes second-hand, from a fan-site retelling of Black Postcards. Wareham also writes of being outvoted by the other two, according to a review of the book at QRO.

No matching account of the LA show from Krukowski or Yang turned up.

eras.title: Maine, then a Monday phone call
eras.text: A campus radio show on April 5, a call on April 8. The accounts of those three days, Wareham's on one side and Krukowski's and Yang's on the other, never quite meet.

years.src: GALAXIE 500 have split (30 years on) · Galaxie 500 have split (35 years on) · Wikipedia: Galaxie 500
years.h: The last show is for 40 or 50 people at Bowdoin College
years.p: April 5, 1991, in Maine for campus station WBOR, after an opener ran long and left the band waiting in the green room.
years.xp:
The show came at the end of a Cocteau Twins tour. Wareham remembers sitting in that green room getting more and more irritated. He says he made it through the set, loaded his gear into his blue 75 Dodge Dart, and drove all the way home to New York City.

Dan Pearson's letter and the Bowdoin Orient are the sources for the show details.

years.big: "Don't buy the tickets to Japan because I was leaving the band."
years.src: GALAXIE 500 have split (30 years on) · Galaxie 500 have split (35 years on) · On Some Bands That Don't Like Each Other I: The Breakup of Galaxie 500
years.h: A Monday call about plane tickets ends Galaxie 500
years.p: On April 8, 1991, Krukowski rang Wareham to book flights for a Japan tour. This is Wareham's account, from Black Postcards.
years.xp:
Krukowski, 1997, to Ptolemaic Terrascope: Wareham quit more or less out of the blue, on the telephone, with no explanation. Melody Maker reported the split on May 4, 1991, quoting Krukowski saying one day they were planning a Japan tour and the next day Wareham just quit.

Naomi Yang, in Temperature's Rising in 2012: she felt completely stripped of her musical identity, and could not believe Wareham could throw everything away so carelessly without wanting to discuss it. In the same account she says she told him he was lazy and a selfish coward.

Wareham, in Black Postcards: he had been up about an hour, with that sick, nervous feeling, and that this time it was real. He writes that he regrets it ended badly, but that is how things often end. Three days of angry phone calls followed.

eras.title: Two answers, and the masters
eras.text: Wareham starts Luna. Krukowski and Yang record as Pierre Etoile, then Damon & Naomi, and later buy the masters back.

years.src: GALAXIE 500 have split (30 years on) · Wikipedia: Galaxie 500
years.h: Krukowski and Yang answer on More Sad Hits
years.p: Their first record without Wareham came out as Pierre Etoile. Asked in 2012 how he felt when Wareham quit, Krukowski pointed to it.
years.xp:
Krukowski, Temperature's Rising, 2012: How did I feel when Dean quit? Are you kidding? Listen to More Sad Hits. Yang told the same magazine it took a long time to recover.

The duo became Damon & Naomi, with the first two records produced by Kramer. They also co-founded the small press Exact Change.

years.h: Wareham spends 1992 on a solo single and Luna's first album
years.p: The single Anesthesia came out in February; [[Luna|dda04604-b50a-4bd1-8780-77564c659dc0]]'s debut, Lunapark, followed the same year.
years.xp: He had also spent time producing Mercury Rev after the split. Luna would run for years, and Wareham would go on to Dean & Britta and a solo record, Foolproof.

years.h: Rough Trade goes bankrupt, and Krukowski and Yang buy the masters
years.p: They bought the three albums' masters at auction in 1996 and reissued them on Rykodisc as a box set with a disc of rarities.
years.xp: The Rykodisc reissue campaign covered all three albums plus rarities. The Portable Galaxie 500 best-of followed in 1998, and Uncollected, more rarities, in 2004.

years.h: The 2004 DVD borrows its title from a Jonathan Richman song
years.p: Don't Let Our Youth Go to Waste, 1987-1991 is two discs of live footage and archive material.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dean Wareham · Dean Wareham : Black Postcards
years.h: Wareham's memoir puts his side of the split in print
years.p: Black Postcards, out on Penguin Press in March 2008, runs from his New York high school years through Galaxie 500 and [[Luna|dda04604-b50a-4bd1-8780-77564c659dc0]] to his divorce.
years.xp: A review at QRO describes him feeling outvoted by Krukowski and Yang, and gives Kramer's wild antics a chapter of their own.

years.h: Wareham goes out playing only Galaxie 500 songs
years.p: He announced the tour in June 2010, without Krukowski and Yang. Neither joined him.
years.xp: Wikipedia's Wareham page dates the tour to 2011; the Galaxie 500 page says he announced it in June 2010 for that autumn.

years.h: Tugboat plays in The Perks of Being a Wallflower
years.p: Stephen Chbosky's film uses the song. Neutral Milk Hotel's Naomi, off On Avery Island, was written about Yang, who made a video for it in 2011.

years.h: Kramer's studio tapes come out as Uncollected Noise New York '88-'90
years.p: The 2024 set collects archival recordings from Noise New York. A live CBGB set dated 12.13.88 was announced for 2025.
